title: The Label and the Lunch Box
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。架空の人物、事例、製品を使った文章であり、実在の制度・調査結果・個別の医療栄養助言ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Two students compare the packages of several snack products in an imaginary classroom activity about food information.
sentences.ja: 二人の生徒は食品情報についての架空授業活動で複数の軽食製品の包装を比較する。

sentences.en: They notice that one package prominently displays a statement about a particular nutrient, while another emphasizes the ingredients from which its contents are made.
sentences.ja: 一包装は特定栄養素の記述を目立たせ、別の包装は中身を作る原材料を強調することに気づく。

sentences.en: Both statements may provide useful information, but neither necessarily describes every characteristic relevant to a person's food choices.
sentences.ja: 両記述は有用情報を提供し得るがどちらも個人の食品選択に関連する全特性を必ずしも記述しない。

sentences.en: The teacher asks the students to distinguish the purpose of a prominent claim from the purpose of a more detailed label.
sentences.ja: 教師は目立つ主張とより詳細な表示の目的を区別させる。

sentences.en: The class examines a fictional example in which a product's advertised quantity of a nutrient refers to a specified portion rather than the entire package.
sentences.ja: 製品が宣伝する栄養素量が包装全体でなく特定の一食分を指す架空例を調べる。

sentences.en: A reader who does not notice the reference amount might misunderstand how the displayed information relates to the quantity of food actually consumed.
sentences.ja: 基準量に気づかない読者は表示情報が実際に摂取する食品量とどう関係するか誤解するかもしれない。

sentences.en: The students therefore consider how information about a product could be compared when the quantities used as a basis for the figures are different.
sentences.ja: そこで数値の基礎として使う量が異なる場合製品情報をどう比較できるか考える。

sentences.en: They recognize that a number becomes interpretable only when its meaning and reference conditions are understood.
sentences.ja: 意味と参照条件が理解されて初めて数値を解釈できると認識する。

sentences.en: Another student points out that a food label may be consulted for reasons other than making comparisons between products.
sentences.ja: 別生徒は食品表示が製品比較以外の理由で参照されることもあると指摘する。

sentences.en: Someone may need to check for a particular ingredient, while another person may be interested in the amount of food contained in a package.
sentences.ja: 特定原材料を確認する必要がある人もいれば包装内の食品量に関心がある人もいる。

sentences.en: The question that a reader is trying to answer determines which parts of the available information require particular attention.
sentences.ja: 読者が答えようとする問いによって情報のどの部分に特に注意が必要か決まる。

sentences.en: The fictional exercise does not recommend particular foods or establish what an individual ought to eat.
sentences.ja: 架空活動は特定食品を推奨せず個人が何を食べるべきかも決定しない。

sentences.en: The students prepare a guide showing how the same imaginary package might be examined by readers with different information needs.
sentences.ja: 情報の必要が異なる読者が同じ仮想包装をどう調べるか示す手引きを作る。

sentences.en: They explain why a prominent claim should be read together with the relevant details rather than interpreted as a complete evaluation of the product.
sentences.ja: 目立つ主張を製品の完全評価と解釈せず関連詳細と一緒に読むべき理由を説明する。

sentences.en: They also distinguish questions that can be answered from the label from questions that require information beyond it.
sentences.ja: 表示で答えられる問いとそれ以外の情報を必要とする問いも区別する。

sentences.en: The activity encourages them to examine information carefully without assuming that every possible food choice can be reduced to a single numerical comparison.
sentences.ja: 活動は全食品選択が一数値比較に還元できると想定せず情報を慎重に調べるよう促す。

sentences.en: Food information can help people make decisions when its meaning is clearly understood.
sentences.ja: 意味が明確に理解されると食品情報は判断を助けられる。

sentences.en: A useful comparison depends on selecting relevant information and recognizing the conditions to which it refers.
sentences.ja: 有用な比較には関連情報の選択とそれが指す条件の認識が必要だ。

sentences.en: The label on a lunch box may answer an important question without answering every question a reader needs to consider.
sentences.ja: 弁当箱の表示は読者が考えるべき全問いに答えずとも重要な問いに答え得る。

sentences.en: Learning what a statement does not tell us is part of learning how to use it responsibly.
sentences.ja: 記述が伝えないことを学ぶのも責任ある利用を学ぶ一部だ。

vocabulary.definition: offer advice about what to do

questions.prompt: What does one package prominently display?
options: A statement about a particular nutrient.
Every possible fact about nutrition.
A detailed exercise plan.
A list of all customers.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish claims from detailed labels?
options: Prominent claims always contain every relevant detail.
Detailed labels are necessarily incorrect.
Food information can never be useful.
Each may serve a different informational purpose.

questions.prompt: What does the fictional nutrient amount refer to?
options: Every product made by the producer.
A specified portion rather than the entire package.
An individual's total diet.
All packages in the shop.

questions.prompt: What could happen if a reader ignores the reference amount?
options: They automatically learn every ingredient.
They determine the product's exact value for everyone.
They may misinterpret how the figure relates to what they eat.
They no longer need any other information.

questions.prompt: What other reason for reading a label is mentioned?
options: Deciding how a classroom is decorated.
Checking whether a particular ingredient is present.
Choosing the size of a school uniform.
Finding the names of every manufacturer.

questions.prompt: Why do different readers focus on different details?
options: They are trying to answer different questions.
Every label provides a different language.
All readers have identical nutritional needs.
Every package has the same contents.

questions.prompt: What does the students' guide demonstrate?
options: An exact recommended diet for every person.
How to remove all labels.
The universal superiority of one product.
Ways readers with different needs might examine the same package.

questions.prompt: Why not treat a prominent claim as a complete evaluation?
options: Prominent claims are necessarily false.
Only a single number can be useful.
Other characteristics may matter to the decision.
A detailed label always determines what everyone should eat.
In a careful manner that considers consequences.
Without thinking about meaning.
In a completely random way.
By ignoring every detail.
A single claim provides all necessary food information.
Useful food information requires understanding its reference conditions and relevance to the reader's question.
Every label gives the same answer to every reader.
Food decisions must depend exclusively on one number.
questions.explanation_ja: 表示の意味と判断目的。

grammar.explanation_ja: neitherは両方否定、necessarilyは必ずしも。

grammar.focus: while another person may be interested
from questions that require information beyond it

paraphrases.source: Both statements may provide useful information, but neither necessarily describes every characteristic relevant to a person's food choices.
paraphrases.rewrite: Neither claim alone necessarily covers everything relevant to a food choice.

paraphrases.source: The class examines a fictional example in which a product's advertised quantity of a nutrient refers to a specified portion rather than the entire package.
paraphrases.rewrite: The advertised amount applies to a specified serving, not necessarily the whole package.

paraphrases.source: Someone may need to check for a particular ingredient, while another person may be interested in the amount of food contained in a package.
paraphrases.rewrite: One reader may check ingredients, whereas another checks quantity.

paraphrases.source: They also distinguish questions that can be answered from the label from questions that require information beyond it.
paraphrases.rewrite: They distinguish questions answered by a label from those needing other information.
